The commit says it fixes exponential backtracking in the footnote-label part of the prefix regex (line 36), but no test guards it. The only footnote row is a single well-formed `[^1]:` label, which the old lazy `\[\^.*?\]:` also handled quickly. The escaped-bracket behaviour the new `(?:\\.|[^\]\\\r\n])*` adds is also untested. For example, `[^a\]: ```suggestion` should now be left alone, since CommonMark treats it as an unterminated label. A guard would be a row with a long run of footnote-like labels and no fence, asserting unchanged output inside a short timeout; dropping the fix would then fail CI rather than hang a review run.

The backtick exemption is guarded by `fence.startsWith("`")`, so a tilde fence with a backtick in its info must still be made inert. No test checks that a tilde fence such as `~~~suggestion` followed by a backtick is still neutralised; that row is the only thing that would catch the `startsWith` guard being dropped.

The comment "A footnote label stops at its first unescaped `]`: one way to split a line of labels, where a lazy match backtracks exponentially." is cryptic: "one way to split" reads as if the code offers one option, and "where" stands in for "whereas". Suggested: "A label ends at its first unescaped `]`, so a line of labels splits only one way; the old lazy `.*?` backtracked exponentially on `[^a]:[^a]:...`."

process_issues.description: Several reviewers' and the validator's first `git -C <path> diff` call hit an approval prompt; each re-ran it as plain `git diff` from the working directory, so no coverage was lost.
